paras: The killing of Josephus Fairchild took place in Lake Charles, Louisiana, shortly before October 1, 1881, when sheriff's deputies shot a Black prisoner who ran from them moments after he was sentenced to death. Struck in the head by a rifle ball, he died in the jail that night. The local Echo's account of the chase, headed "A Race for Life," was reprinted as far away as Wisconsin.

A grand jury had indicted Fairchild, described as "a short but strongly-built negro," for the murder of "a negro named Frank Clout" near Lake Charles the previous spring. Arrested in Rapides Parish, he was brought back from Alexandria by Deputy Sheriff John S. Hawkins. A jury convicted him, and District Judge S. D. Read ordered him brought into court for sentencing with his handcuffs and shackles removed.

Four deputies attended him, one of them, Richard Coward, carrying a Winchester rifle. As a deputy led him out after the death sentence, Fairchild broke free on the front steps and ran. Coward and another deputy fired as he crossed the roadside ditch, and he fell, rose, and ran past the jail under what the Echo called "a perfect storm of bullets." On Ryan street a ball from Coward's rifle struck him behind the left ear; carried unconscious to the jail, he died between 10 and 11 o'clock that night.
No report of an inquest or of any inquiry into the shooting appears in the coverage.

The Donaldsonville Chief ran the news on October 1 among Louisiana crime briefs, saying Fairchild was fired upon after "refusing to halt." The fuller Echo story ran in the Mineral Point Tribune on October 6 and the River Falls Journal on October 13 as the "Desperate Attempt of a Louisiana Murderer to Escape from Four Officers." Both versions came from the officers' side and treated the shooting as a dramatic escape attempt, the Echo writing that Fairchild "of course, fell headlong."
The Echo account dates the scene both to "last Tuesday" and to "last Friday"; the Donaldsonville report shows only that it occurred before October 1.

reader.title: Killing of Josephus Fairchild
bases: Sheriff's deputies shot and killed a Black prisoner who ran from them on the courthouse steps after his death sentence; no crowd took part (A1, A2).

A Louisiana state-news brief (A1) and the Lake Charles Echo account reprinted in Wisconsin (A2, A3) agree on the sentencing, the break, the deputies' fire and the death that night, though both probably derive from Lake Charles sources and give only the officers' side.

accounts.label: Lake Charles Echo (local paper, officers' side)
accounts.gist: After sentencing, Fairchild threw off a deputy's grasp on the courthouse steps and ran; Coward and another deputy fired, he fell, rose and ran on under heavy fire until Coward's rifle ball struck his head on Ryan street; he died in jail that night.

accounts.label: Louisiana state-news brief
accounts.gist: Fairchild broke for liberty while being taken back to jail and, 'refusing to halt', was fired on by four deputies and mortally wounded.

framing.detail: The Donaldsonville Chief explained the shooting by his 'refusing to halt' and filed it among routine state crime items.

The Echo account, reprinted under 'A Race for Life. Desperate Attempt of a Louisiana Murderer to Escape from Four Officers', told it as a 'thrilling scene' and wrote that he 'of course, fell headlong'.
